title: fix: cuda-graph shape-guard warmup regression for attention kernels
author: Maria Chen
description: This PR addresses a regression introduced during the recent CUDA graph capture/replay refactor that caused warmup shape guards to be incorrectly cached for attention kernels, producing incorrect kernel selection on replays and visible latency spikes under multi-shape workloads. Root cause: the shape-guard key used by the graph warmup path did not include sequence-length-on-device after KV cache path change, which meant captures for one sequence shape were reused for different KV layouts. Fix: ensure warmup shape-guard keys include dynamic KV layout descriptors and add an additional sanity-check at replay time to re-capture when mismatch detected. Also add defensive logging and a unit test that simulates alternating sequence lengths to prevent regression. Testing: unit tests added, integration canary in perf-lab ran across weight-shared models and showed stable latency distribution; CI flaky attention-kernel test was stabilized by increasing synthetic batch jitter tolerance. Backport: small patch should be cherry-picked to release/2026-02 for customers on Dedicated with pinned runtimes. Checklist: [x] reproduce regression locally; [x] add unit + integration tests; [x] add changelog and backport notes; [x] CI green and perf canary observed.
commits_summary: 1) fix(warmup): include kv_layout in shape-guard key and runtime sanity checks; 2) test: add warmup replay multi-shape unit and deterministic kernel selection test; 3) logging: add debug logs for capture/replay mismatches; 4) docs: add brief note in serving/runtime/CHANGELOG about regression and backport
